newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 5.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 5.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to large ships on Thursday as Tropical Storm Andres' force waned, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.
Strong winds along the Pacific Coast shut the largely tourist ports of Huatulco and Puerto Madero to smaller tourism and fishing craft.
The SCT warned ships of high winds and waves along the coasts of Chiapas and Oaxaca because of Andres.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Weak cold front crossing Baja California and carrying light rains to region. Winds in the north from 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves five to eight feet high.
Along the southern coast, Andres was 21 miles (34 km) southeast of Puerto Madero, Chiapas state, spurring winds from 35 to 40 knots (66 to 76 km/38 to 44 miles) and waves to 12 feet high.
Andres switched direction early Thursday, moving toward the east. The report said it expected the storm to hit land later in the day and lose force.
Light rains expected later in the day on the coasts of Veracruz, Tabasco and the Yucatan peninsula. Winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves three to six feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with rains and strong winds in Quintana Roo state. Winds from 20 to 30 km (12 to 19 miles) per hour with gusts of up to 35 km (22 miles).
